instruction.name: xvdiv.b
instruction.description: Divide each signed 8-bit element in `a` by the corresponding element in `b`.

experiments.name: operand dependency chain
experiments.init: li.d $r4, 1; xvreplgr2vr.b $xr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; xvreplgr2vr.b $xr1, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; xvreplgr2vr.b $xr2, $r4

latencies.notes: xj -> result chain. Data-dependent: latency = 5 + 6*8 + 16*quotient_bits/8 = 53 + 8*floor(bits/4) for a 8-bit element. Min 29 with a zero dividend, max 61 at a 7-bit quotient. LSX and LASX are identical for every element width although LASX carries twice the lanes, so the lanes (and both 128-bit halves) are refined in parallel and only the element width sets the per-bit rate. Measured with divisor 1, where the quotient equals the dividend, so the chain holds its operand constant and needs no helper.

throughput.notes: Range over the same pairs: min CPI 13.50 at 0/1, max CPI 29.50 at 127/1. Sample uses 1/1.

notes: LASX variable-latency integer divide/modulo. Latency uses an element-0 reset helper; throughput uses 8 independent lanes. Ranges cover positive operands including powers of two and max values. Both vector sources are recorded separately; they share the same result path where the hardware is symmetric.
